claims.statement: Binding Tariff Information is a legal classification decision issued by EU customs authorities, generally valid across the EU for three years and binding on authorities and the holder.
Tariff classification determines customs duty and can also determine non-tariff measures such as licences, restrictions and origin-related requirements.

In Poland, a WIT application and decision are electronic and free; paid value must therefore come from complex fact development, expert review and workflow support rather than access to the official filing itself.

After a complete BTI application is accepted, the authority normally has 120 days to decide, with exceptional extensions possible; a decision based on inaccurate or incomplete applicant information is annulled.
Commercial incumbents already offer AI-assisted or automated tariff classification, bulk processing, APIs, reasoning and human-expert review.
Maersk already offers European HS-classification consulting and customs-clearance support, so a freight forwarder can be both a channel and a direct substitute.

The defensible wedge is more likely a confidential, expert-reviewed evidence and exception workflow for difficult products than a generic code recommender, because official rulings are public and code automation is already crowded.

contrary_evidence: Valid and invalid BTI decisions are already public in the EBTI database, so defensibility must come from confidential fact patterns, workflow distribution and outcome data rather than public rulings.
The official Polish WIT application and decision are free, so the proposed case fee cannot be justified by filing access alone.
Avalara, eClear and TariffPilot already automate classification research and workflow, including APIs, bulk processing and human expertise.
Maersk already sells HS-classification consulting alongside customs clearance, creating channel conflict with a forwarder-embedded product.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated hypothesis: use low-volume, account-based outreach to customs and compliance owners in one evidence-selected importer vertical; treat forwarders and customs agents only as non-exclusive referrals or integration endpoints. No evidence establishes conversion, sales cycle, acquisition cost, or reachable account density.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: No source-backed forecast or timing estimate is possible for the redesigned model. Hypothesis, not evidence: recurring direct contracts plus a permissioned vertical workflow asset could create founder equity and retained cash. Intermediate proof gates are a paid pilot, annual renewal, repeatable acquisition, positive contribution economics, and scalable expert delivery; contract value, account count, margins, retention, acquisition cost, valuation, and the path to 5 million PLN remain unknown.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated: the model fits the founder limit only if contracted customs specialists own professional judgments, representation, and escalations while the founder owns product, data, and batched account acquisition. The direct-sales workload is unknown.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated hypothesis: annual monitoring and reusable vertical fact templates may spread expert cost across repeated cases. Actual expert hours, insurance, liability, support load, and realised margin are unknown; the earlier 55%-80% range is not treated as evidence.
economics.payback: Unknown. Direct importer contracting removes dependence on a forwarder revenue share or embed but introduces unmeasured outreach, sales-cycle, and onboarding costs; payback must be observed in paid pilots.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: an annual monitoring and workflow contract plus a separate fee for difficult expert-reviewed cases. No price level is asserted; willingness to pay and packaging must be established through paid pilots.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated hypothesis: annual renewal follows repeated new-SKU intake, rule changes, disputes, and accumulated product history within one vertical. Renewal rate, case frequency, and the incremental value of monitoring are unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned vertical-specific product-fact templates, review questions, decisions, rule-change impacts, and realised case outcomes may reduce expert effort and increase renewal value, but compound only if customers grant reuse rights and outcomes accumulate
fingerprint.customer: EU importers in a single repeat-SKU product vertical to be selected only after direct evidence of recurring difficult-classification loss and insufficient internal capability
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct account-based outreach to customs and compliance owners in one evidence-selected importer vertical; forwarders and customs agents are non-exclusive referral or integration endpoints rather than the indispensable channel
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Direct annual importer contract for vertical-specific product-fact intake, expert-reviewed classification evidence, rule-change monitoring, and exception or appeal workflow, with qualified professionals owning advice and representation
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer pays for an annual classification-assurance renewal and for expert review when a difficult new SKU or dispute requires a defensible evidence pack; both paid events remain unvalidated hypotheses
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new SKU lacks a defensible tariff classification or faces a classification dispute

founder_fit: A single vertical and structured product-fact workflow fit the founder data, AI, and automation strengths.

Owning direct importer accounts removes the forwarder as an indispensable channel, but direct B2B acquisition may still consume substantial social energy; the workload and ability to systematize it are unvalidated.

Qualified customs professionals can be contracted in the proposed structure while the founder builds product and data systems, but specialist availability, cost, insurance, and liability allocation remain unknown.
The inherited 75,000 PLN capital estimate is within stated free capital but remains unvalidated and should be staged behind paid demand evidence.

redesign.economic_effect: Evidence from the cited research: forwarders can sell classification themselves; official filing is free; public sources and incumbent tools commoditise simple research; and no evidence validates direct importer contracts, case volume, pricing, data rights, margins, or retention. Hypothesis: owning the annual importer relationship in one evidence-selected vertical removes the forwarder as an indispensable gatekeeper, concentrates repeat cases, lets monitoring and reusable fact templates spread expert and acquisition cost, and makes permissioned data reuse more controllable. These effects remain unvalidated until paid pilots, renewals, contribution margins, and signed data rights are observed.

risks: The selected vertical may lack enough repeat difficult-case density to support annual contracts.
Direct importer acquisition may create a slow, socially demanding sales cycle incompatible with part-time operation.
Incorrect or incomplete product facts may lead to an invalid or harmful classification.
Customers may refuse outcome-data reuse, leaving no proprietary learning asset.
Public AI tools and mature managed-service incumbents may commoditise the workflow or outcompete the offer.
The slow official BTI cycle may delay verified outcomes and weaken the proposed data flywheel.
Acting as a customs representative without proper empowerment or applicable national conditions may create liability.
Qualified-expert review, insurance, and escalations may keep delivery service-heavy and constrain margin.

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical managed-compliance subscription with expert escalation and a permissioned case-learning asset
structure.control_point: Direct importer renewal relationship and, only when contractually granted, rights to reuse de-identified vertical product-fact, decision, and monitoring outcomes
structure.critical_dependency: Direct evidence that one importer vertical has sufficient repeat difficult-case volume and willingness to pay, plus qualified expert capacity and explicit data-use rights; none is yet validated

thesis: Sell an annual expert-backed classification evidence and monitoring contract directly to importers in one initially selected repeat-SKU vertical. The importer relationship, rather than a forwarder, is the primary distribution and renewal point; forwarders and customs agents are optional referral or integration endpoints. Qualified customs professionals remain responsible for advice and representation, and de-identified case reuse occurs only under explicit contractual permission. The target vertical, willingness to pay, case density, margins, renewal, and data rights remain unvalidated.
title: Importer-Owned Vertical Classification Assurance
uncertainties: Which single product vertical has documented classification-loss exposure, repeated difficult-SKU volume, and insufficient internal classification capability
Importer willingness to buy and renew an annual contract or pay separately for difficult expert-reviewed cases
Direct-account conversion, sales cycle, acquisition cost, and reachable account density
Qualified customs-specialist cost, availability, insurance, and liability allocation
Exact Polish conditions when the service crosses from research support into customs representation
Contractual permission to reuse de-identified product facts, questions, appeals, decisions, and landed-cost outcomes
Whether a narrow vertical workflow is materially faster, safer, or more accurate than incumbent managed services
Annual renewal, case frequency, and monitoring value
